rounds.text: Conceded: [E16]. Despite headline growth figures, investors receive no cash return on their investment, as evidenced by a dividend yield of exactly 0.00% [E4]. Furthermore, the underlying business operations carry notable vulnerability to timing risks, with approximately 55% of annual revenue concentrated in the second half of the year and over 30% arriving in the fourth quarter alone [E74]. This heavy seasonal skew creates severe working capital pressures and forecasting hazards. Compounding this operational friction, top-line expansion directly generates a higher receivable base to support increased customer activity [E75], pointing to potential cash conversion headwinds that could strain liquidity as scale increases. Finally, the stock trades at a price-to-book multiple of 1.98x on a book value of ₹ 46.0 [E2], a premium valuation that leaves little margin for error should the anticipated capacity utilization ramp stall.

Conceded: [E4]. The bear's concern regarding seasonal concentration is overstated, given that this predictable second-half weighting of 55% of annual revenue is paired with proven multi-year sales compounding of 32% [E14, E15, E74]. The criticism that higher receivables create liquidity strain ignores the fact that this is a natural consequence of supporting surging customer activity alongside exceptional 3-year profit growth of 122% and trailing profit growth of 67% [E16, E17, E75]. Furthermore, the premium-valuation critique overlooks that a P/E of 12.5x is exceptionally modest relative to a massive 122% profit growth rate and a sector benchmark of 21.26x [E1, E6, E16]. Finally, the fear of a stalled capacity utilization ramp is neutralized by the 47% available headroom in existing facilities, which supports embedded growth without major capex while driving toward an anticipated 65% utilization target by the end of the fiscal year [E62, E78].

Conceded: [E14, E15, E16, E17, E62]. The bull dismisses the operational risks of seasonality by pointing to multi-year growth, but an annual business model where 55% of revenue and over 30% of fourth-quarter sales concentrate in the second half creates severe cash flow friction and earnings visibility risks [E74]. This uneven collection profile directly feeds into the growing receivable base, which management admits is a natural consequence of chasing volume rather than enforcing disciplined cash conversion [E75]. The bull's reliance on a 12.5x P/E ratio and sector comparisons ignores the complete absence of shareholder returns, as the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield [E1, E4, E6]. Finally, the projection of reaching 65% capacity utilization by the end of the fiscal year still leaves substantial unutilized headroom in a facility already generating high receivables to sustain its sales push [E62, E75, E78].
